record.context_brief: Natural dissipation in direct cascade models
record.original_question: In an infinite mechanical model intended to produce a direct energy cascade through families of balls, can energy dissipation be introduced in a natural way without explicitly adding friction or an artificial far-away energy sink?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite one-dimensional mechanical system designed to model a direct energy cascade. The system consists of a sequence (indexed by n = 0, 1, 2, ...) of families of perfectly elastic balls, where balls in the n-th family have mass m_n and characteristic length scale L_n with m_n -> 0 and L_n -> 0 as n -> infinity. Energy is injected at the largest scale (n = 0) and is transferred through elastic collisions to balls of progressively smaller scales, mimicking the transfer of kinetic energy from large to small scales in three-dimensional turbulence.

Question: Is it possible to introduce energy dissipation into such an infinite mechanical model in a natural way, intrinsic to the dynamics of the system itself, without explicitly adding a friction (damping) force to the equations of motion and without postulating an artificial energy sink located "at infinity" (i.e., absorbing energy that has cascaded down to arbitrarily small scales)?

In other words, can the limit n -> infinity of the family of finite truncations of the model be taken in such a way that the resulting infinite system exhibits genuine energy dissipation as an emergent property of its purely conservative collisional dynamics?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2022/2023 collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics, where it is explicitly listed as an unresolved question concerning natural dissipation mechanisms in infinite mechanical cascade models. No subsequent resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (arXiv:2205.01143)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics including mechanical cascade models with balls and questions about natural energy dissipation.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in this collection.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems - ARMA
status_evidence.snippet: Published in Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis (2023) as a survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Listed among the open problems with no announced solution.
